mn_fern_gully.blurb: A small, in-town bouldering spot in Duluth's Lincoln Park neighbourhood, tucked into the woods beside a creek and named for the ferns that carpet the ground. Thirteen problems are known, and the bulk of them sit between V1 and V3, so it suits people building up. A few much harder lines top out around V6 and V7. It is a quick stop rather than a full day out, with a cliff band visible soon after you enter the trees and a lower band beneath it. A few more new lines are thought possible.

mn_kanaranzi_buttress_south_face.blurb: A south-facing quartzite buttress in the North Quarry section of Blue Mounds State Park, close to Luverne on the Minnesota prairie. Thirteen routes are recorded, mostly top-rope with a handful of trad lines, running from easy fifth class up to 5.11. Most fall in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, so there is something for solid intermediates as well as a few harder tests. Protection tends to be spaced out, so bring plenty of slings for building anchors. Bolted lines are not the norm in this park.

mn_pot_holes_area.blurb: Part of Interstate State Park at Taylors Falls on the St. Croix River, this is a compact section reached on foot from the main lot. Climbing here is traditional, top-rope and bouldering, with no bolted sport lines and a clean-climbing ethic. Of thirteen climbs, roughly half are trad, a few are boulder problems and a couple are top-ropes. Expect short but stiff routes: mostly 5.10 range, with a few at 5.12 and one 5.13, plus easy V2 problems and a pair of very hard boulders. A path forks toward two different walls.

mn_main_flow_area_2.blurb: The north end of the Sandstone Ice Park in Robinson Park, in the town of Sandstone, and a winter-only venue. Ice here is partly natural and largely farmed, so quality depends on the weather and on how well the flows have been maintained. The dozen climbs split between ice, mixed and dry-tooling style sport lines. Ice runs about WI3 to WI4, mixed lines run M5 to M7, and the dry routes sit around 5.10 to 5.13. Expect mostly top-rope setups on short walls.

mn_avery_boulder.blurb: A small bouldering spot in Duluth, off the beaten path and hard to spot among trees. Twelve problems are recorded, mostly between VB and V2 with a few up to V5. The holds are small pockets and pinches with good friction, which can be hard on skin and fingers, while landings are flat and top-outs are solid. It is a relatively new area, with unclimbed lines said to remain, best for a short session combined with other Duluth stops.
